headline: Highest risk is CrewAI’s default shared-memory, filesystem, and broad egress creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure with nuwa-skill.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory in a crew, so attacker-controlled content can bridge into another agent’s context. nuwa-skill exposes allowlisted egress but no isolation details, so the pairwise path is plausible yet not directly documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, prompt-like content in files can influence downstream agent behavior.
IF nuwa-skill consumes CrewAI-produced text as instructions, injected directives can propagate.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable file-based handoff between agents.
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in all shared artifacts.
Review any file content before passing it to the other agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and reads/writes the host working directory; nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress. If sensitive crew data reaches nuwa-skill, leakage can occur through its outbound calls. The exact shared workspace is undocumented, so I choose medium rather than low because the default CrewAI surface is broad.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace, files containing secrets can be read by CrewAI and then forwarded by nuwa-skill.
IF nuwa-skill sends received content to external services, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Run nuwa-skill with a minimal allowlist.
Redact API keys before handoff.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has broad filesystem write and subprocess execution, while nuwa-skill only documents allowlisted egress. There is no documented overlapping write target or shared mutable resource, so a direct capability conflict is not established. Because the interaction is underdocumented, I avoid none but keep it low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable resource, their actions can race.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Disable write access for one agent where possible.
Serialize writes through a single coordinator.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew and shared memory make its outputs likely to be treated as authoritative inside the pair, while nuwa-skill’s research-oriented role suggests it may consume those outputs for further action. No verification step is documented, so a mistaken CrewAI output can cascade into nuwa-skill’s downstream behavior.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill uses CrewAI output as input without validation, errors can propagate.
IF CrewAI generates incorrect facts that nuwa-skill reuses, downstream outputs may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a verification step before reuse.
Ask nuwa-skill to cite source evidence separately.
Compare outputs against original inputs.
Flag low-confidence claims for manual review.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, but nuwa-skill has no documented sensitive-data classes or residency constraints. With no evidence of a specific residency or certification mismatch, only a limited compliance gap is plausible, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into CrewAI and then into nuwa-skill, policy review is required.
IF either agent logs retained sensitive inputs, retention policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Check logging settings for both agents.
Set short retention on any transcripts.
Document the data flow before deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
